note: What each workshop app's planner receives. `problem` is what the participant types (short, in their words); `facilitator_brief` is the minimal steering, shown to participants as "Facilitator's brief". Written 2 Nov 2026.

s7-1-dashboard.title: Your country's recommendations dashboard
s7-1-dashboard.problem: I need to see what UN human rights mechanisms have told my country, on which themes and when, find the exact paragraphs fast, and know whether I can trust the numbers.
s7-1-dashboard.facilitator_brief: A dashboard on the participant's country's file from the Universal Human Rights Index. It should be trustworthy enough for a diplomat preparing a meeting: every number explained, and every paragraph one click from its UN document.

s7-4-extract.title: Paragraphs out of a UN document
s7-4-extract.problem: Our office copies paragraphs out of UN documents by hand. Can a tool turn a General Comment into a clean list of numbered paragraphs we can cite and reuse, and show me where it may have got things wrong?
s7-4-extract.facilitator_brief: The file is CESCR General comment No. 27 as OHCHR publishes it in HTML, with a reference (paragraph count, footnote count, first words of each paragraph). The tool must check itself against the reference, say what the HTML version lacks, and let us take the paragraphs away as a dataset, in JSON and Markdown.

s8-1-verbatim.title: Verbatim finder for General Comments
s8-1-verbatim.problem: When I draft a submission I need the exact words of General Comments on my topic, a correct citation, and a place to collect the passages I want. Help me find them.
s8-1-verbatim.facilitator_brief: A search tool over every General Comment paragraph of the treaty bodies: it retrieves, it never generates. Boolean search and exact phrases, citations ready to paste, and a way to collect quotations for a draft.

s8-5-wiki.title: A research wiki on neurotechnology and justice
s8-5-wiki.problem: Our team keeps losing track of what each report says about neurotechnology in the justice system. Build us a research wiki we can ask questions of, add new reports to, and trust: every quote checked against its source.
s8-5-wiki.facilitator_brief: The wiki is already compiled from nine sources (WORKSHOP_DATA.wiki), following Karpathy's LLM-wiki pattern as kept in a book project: source, concept, entity and question pages, verified pins that open the PDF page, registers and contested claims. The app is the team's workspace for it: read and navigate, Ask the wiki and file good answers back, Ingest the waiting source A/HRC/57/61 with a human approving each change, and Lint. The model drafts; the code verifies every quotation.
